newsitem.title: POLAND: Stalexport sees surge in 1997 profits.
newsitem.headline: Stalexport sees surge in 1997 profits.

text.p: Poland's steel trader and producer expects its net profit to rise to 40-50 million zlotys this year from last year's 25.6 million zlotys, the company's president said on Tuesday.

"In 1997 we predict net sales of two billion zlotys and a net profit of 40-50 million zlotys," Ryszard Harhala told a news conference. Harhala said Stalexport saw its sales rising from 1.63 billion in 1996.
He said the company expected to step up exports of steel products manufactured by its subsidiaries and other products.
Harhala said that because of weak European markets Stalexport saw better opportunites in the Far East.
"Because prices continue to stay low in Europe the company plans to step up its sales in Malaysia and Singapore," he said.
Harhala said another prospective area of growth was Poland's motorway construction programme in which Stalexport wanted to participate as supplier and administrator of toll routes.

He said he expected the transport ministry to award within weeks a Stalexport-led consortium a licence to operate a 70-kilometre stretch of toll motorway linking the southern cities of Katowice and Krakow.

Harhala said Stalexport, with its minority French partner Transroute Internationale, was seeking a 35-year licence, which could bring 10 million zlotys annualy in toll revenues with initial investment estimated at $27-30 million.
